surfaces.part: line of weeds, rosettes and flowers along a diagonal crack, drawn as a flat ground decal seen from above

answer.evidence: The silhouette is an irregular organic scatter of leaves, rosettes and small flowers (widths 2-16 across rows 0-15) lying along a diagonal crack. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no vertical south face of 3 or more rows. It is a flat ground decal seen from above, which matches the flat kind, so it reads as top_down_slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate renders very small on the board, so I judged it by eye as a sparse decal-style ground piece. It still reads as a dense cluster of leaf and rosette shapes in several greens, with a few yellow and pink flower dots. Measured facts support this: about 25 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving. Near-flat coverage is 0%, with no 5x5 flat blocks. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the shadows lean dark green rather than black, which fits the Beodeul habit of using the adjacent material's dark tone instead of a sticker outline. Leaf clumps are shaded in roughly 4-5 steps, comparable to the reference foliage texture. The weakness is the small footprint. It does not show the full 4x3 diagonal crack, so I could not judge the crack's soil structure. On the evidence of the visible pixels, it is not thinner or flatter than the references.
